summary: Bonner County, Idaho lookout on Kaniksu NF: an L-4 cab (1930), then a 40-ft L-4 tower (1940s) that blew down in 1953; a 2023 post says ruins of both towers remain.

facts.design: L-4 cab (1930), then 40-ft pole tower with L-4 cab (1940s)
facts.status_note: Tower blew down in 1953; an Idaho Fire Lookouts post says the ruins of both L-4 towers remain on the summit

access.note: Reached on foot from Lunch Peak per an Idaho Fire Lookouts post, which encourages the trip and mentions no closure or permit; no official access rule found

visit.trail_note: Hike from Lunch Peak; the post says the trail is in great shape

events.note: Northern Idaho News item dated April 16, 1929, quoted on Forest Lookouts: a new station to be erected on Pend d'Oreille peak at the head of Lightning creek (original newspaper not checked)
L-4 cab built, per all three sites
Tower blew down, per all three sites; the 1940s tower is the one that fell

evidence.supports: 1930 L-4 cab; 1940s 40-ft L-4 tower; blew down 1953; Kaniksu National Forest
evidence.quote: 1930: L-4 cab. 1940s: 40' pole L-4 tower. Blew down 1953.

evidence.supports: ruins of both L-4 towers remain on the summit (2023 post)
evidence.quote: The ruins from both L-4 towers are still here.

evidence.supports: earlier cab ruins are just down the ridge, mostly wood planks; the later tower's fall is clearly visible
evidence.quote: The ruins from the 1930s L-4 is also easy to find just down the ridge although its mostly just wood planks.

evidence.supports: the spot where the 1940s tower blew over is clearly visible
evidence.quote: You can clearly see where the 1940s tower blew over

the trail is gorgeous and in great shape!

evidence.quote: we highly encourage everyone visiting Lunch Peak to make the short trek over!

sources.title: Mt. Pend Oreille Fire Lookout Tower

notes_for_editor: Dates agree across the three lookout sites (1930 cab, 1940s tower, 1953 blow-down), but they appear to share one Kresek-attributed inventory. The 1940s date is decade-only, so it is not recorded as an event. The ruins description comes from one post dated 2023-08-17 on Idaho Fire Lookouts; no newer visit report or Forest Service access rule was found. The 1929 newspaper quote is as printed on the Forest Lookouts page; the original newspaper was not checked. The brief's height_m of 12.2 m matches the 40-ft 1940s tower, the last one standing before it fell. The brief's record had no events; the 1929, 1930 and 1953 events are added.
